data.stem: The proposal that India should have a Constituent Assembly was first made in 1934 by:
data.explanation: M. N. Roy is correct; the communist pioneer floated the idea in 1934. Nehru only voiced the Congress position in 1938, Gandhi was not even a member of the Assembly, and Cripps brought a British draft plan in 1942, so these options are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Britain first conceded, in principle, that Indians should frame their own constitution through which of these?
data.explanation: The August Offer of 1940 is correct, being the first in-principle acceptance. The Cripps Proposals (1942) and the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) came later and built on it, whereas the Mountbatten Plan dealt with partition, so the other options are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly as planned by the Cabinet Mission:
1. Its total strength was fixed at 389.
2. Seats were given roughly in the ratio of one for every million people.
3. Princely-state members were to be directly elected by the people of those states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct: the scheme fixed 389 seats and used about one seat per million population. Statement 3 is wrong because the rulers of the princely states nominated their members, so every option that includes 3 is incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Under the 1946 scheme, by what method did provincial legislators choose members of the Constituent Assembly?
options: Direct election on universal adult franchise
Proportional representation by single transferable vote
data.explanation: Single transferable vote is correct: each community's members in the provincial assembly elected their share through proportional representation by STV. First-past-the-post was not used, nomination applied only to princely states, and adult franchise is wrong because the election was indirect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: How many of the 296 British-Indian seats did the Congress secure in the Assembly elections of July–August 1946?
data.explanation: 208 is correct. 73 is wrong because it was the Muslim League's tally; 229 is wrong because it was the provinces' strength after partition; and 163 is incorrect since it was the number of Hindu members in the community-wise breakdown.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Who presided over the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly on 9 December 1946?
data.explanation: Sachchidananda Sinha is correct; as the oldest member he acted as temporary chairman, following French practice. Rajendra Prasad became permanent President two days later, Mukherjee was a Vice-President, and Mavalankar chaired only the legislative sittings, so these are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Arrange in chronological order:
1. Election of Rajendra Prasad as permanent President
2. Moving of the Objectives Resolution
3. Adoption of the Objectives Resolution
4. Setting up of the Drafting Committee
Select the correct order:
data.explanation: 1, 2, 3, 4 is correct: Prasad was elected on 11 Dec 1946, Nehru moved the Resolution on 13 Dec 1946, it was adopted on 22 Jan 1947, and the Drafting Committee came on 29 Aug 1947. The other sequences misplace at least one of these dates and are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: A modified form of which document now appears as the Preamble to the Constitution?
options: The Cabinet Mission statement of 16 May 1946
data.explanation: The Objectives Resolution is correct; Nehru moved it in December 1946 and its adapted text became the Preamble. The Lahore resolution explains only why 26 January was chosen, and the Cabinet Mission statement merely set up the Assembly, so those are incorrect, as is the Nehru Report.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding changes made by the Indian Independence Act, 1947 to the Constituent Assembly:
1. The Assembly could alter or abolish any British law relating to India.
2. The Assembly also began to act as the legislature of the Dominion.
3. The total membership rose above 389 when princely states joined.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct: the Act made the Assembly sovereign and also its first Parliament. Statement 3 is wrong; membership actually fell to 299 after League members from Pakistan areas withdrew, so options with 3 are incorrect, and '1 only' misses a true statement.
data.label: practice

data.stem: When the Constituent Assembly sat as the Dominion Legislature, who chaired those sittings?
data.explanation: G. V. Mavalankar is correct; he was elected Speaker when the body first met as a legislature on 17 November 1947. Prasad chaired only the constitution-making days, Nehru was Prime Minister, and Krishnamachari was the second Vice-President, so those answers are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: After partition, the Assembly's membership stood at 299. How was this divided?
data.explanation: 229 and 70 is correct: provincial seats dropped from 296 and princely seats from 93. The 296/93 pair is wrong because it was the original 1946 allocation, and 208 is the Congress tally, not a seat category; the last pair is simply incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following was NOT done by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950?
options: Electing Dr Rajendra Prasad as the first President
data.explanation: The national flag is the right NOT answer, since it was adopted much earlier, on 22 July 1947. The anthem, the national song and the election of Prasad as President all took place on 24 January 1950, so those options are wrong choices here.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Match the committee with its chairman:
A. Provincial Constitution Committee
B. Union Powers Committee
C. Steering Committee
D. Drafting Committee
1. Rajendra Prasad  2. B. R. Ambedkar  3. Sardar Patel  4. Jawaharlal Nehru
data.explanation: A-3, B-4, C-1, D-2 is correct: Patel led the Provincial Constitution Committee, Nehru the Union Powers Committee, Prasad the Steering Committee and Ambedkar the Drafting Committee. The other codes swap Nehru, Patel or Prasad and are therefore incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: The Minorities Sub-Committee under the Advisory Committee was headed by:
data.explanation: H. C. Mukherjee is correct. Kripalani is wrong because he led the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee; Bardoloi headed the north-east tribal and Assam excluded areas body; and Thakkar led the sub-committee on other excluded areas, so these are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of these people was NOT a member of the Drafting Committee as finally constituted?
data.explanation: Sardar Patel is the correct NOT answer; he chaired other committees but never sat on the seven-member Drafting Committee. Ayyangar and Saadullah were original members, and Krishnamachari joined after D. P. Khaitan's death, so they are wrong answers.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following statements about the drafting process:
1. The Drafting Committee was constituted on 29 August 1947.
2. Its first draft was published in February 1948.
3. The public was given two months to suggest changes to that draft.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct. Statement 3 is wrong because people had eight months, not two, to discuss the first draft before a second draft appeared in October 1948; therefore options containing statement 3 are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: During the clause-by-clause second reading of the draft, roughly how many amendments were tabled?
data.explanation: 7,653 is correct; members tabled that many amendments, of which 2,473 were actually discussed. So 2,473 is wrong as the tabled figure, 395 is wrong because it is the original number of Articles, and 1,141 is incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem: In its original form, as adopted on 26 November 1949, the Constitution contained:
data.explanation: A Preamble, 395 Articles and 8 Schedules is correct. Twelve Schedules and a higher Article count reflect later amendments, so those options are wrong, and 389 is incorrect because it is the Assembly's original seat strength, not an Article count.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Why was 26 January selected as the day on which the Constitution would come into force?
options: The Constituent Assembly first met on that date
India became a Dominion on that date
The Objectives Resolution was adopted on that date
Purna Swaraj day had been observed on that date in 1930
data.explanation: Purna Swaraj is correct: after the Lahore Congress of December 1929, 26 January 1930 was celebrated as independence day. The Assembly first met on 9 December 1946, India became a Dominion on 15 August 1947, and the Resolution passed on 22 January 1947, so the rest are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which of the following provisions took effect on 26 November 1949 rather than on 26 January 1950?
options: Provisions on the Union executive's powers
data.explanation: Citizenship and elections is correct; Articles 5–9 and 324, along with the provisional Parliament, transitional rules and short title, began on the day of adoption. Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles and the Union executive formed part of the bulk that started in 1950, so they are wrong.
data.label: practice

data.stem: Which law was NOT repealed when the Constitution commenced, but was allowed to continue?
options: Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949
Acts amending the Government of India Act, 1935
data.explanation: The Abolition of Privy Council Jurisdiction Act, 1949 is correct; it stayed in force. The 1935 Act, the 1947 Independence Act and all statutes amending or supplementing the 1935 Act were repealed on commencement, so the other options are incorrect.
data.label: practice

data.stem:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Constitutional adviser to the Assembly – B. N. Rau
2. Calligrapher of the original Constitution – Prem Behari Narain Raizada
3. Chief draftsman – H. V. R. Iyengar
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
data.explanation: 1 and 2 only is correct: B. N. Rau advised the Assembly and Raizada hand-wrote the Constitution. Pair 3 is wrong because Iyengar was the Assembly's Secretary, whereas S. N. Mukherjee was the chief draftsman, so options including 3 are incorrect.
data.label: practice
